children: reported a quarter powered by stronger demand, with shares at $165.65, up 5.62% from the previous close, around 10.59 a.m. ET on October 22. Fiscal first-quarter sales climbed 4% to $23.3 billion, while organic sales also rose 4%. The encouraging part: shoppers bought more. Volume contributed roughly 2.4 percentage points to growth, versus just 0.4 point from pricing.

Cash generation stayed strong. Operating cash flow reached $5.8 billion, supporting $3.9 billion in dividends and buybacks. But sales growth did not translate into much earnings growth: diluted earnings rose just 1% to $1.97 a share as operating costs increased. According to Reuters, higher raw-material, energy and freight costs remain a drag on the annual profit outlook. More products leaving shelves helps. Keeping enough profit on each sale is the harder job.

The valuation leaves little room for disappointment: $165.65 sits just 1.44% below the $168.07 GF Value estimate, suggesting only a slim discount. Volume growth gives investors something tangible to cheer, but modest earnings growth keeps the pressure on margins. Sustaining demand, containing costs and integrating Thorne now matter more than another round of price increases.

title: Procter & Gamble Stocks Gain 5.62% on Volume-Led Quarter
